title: iDRAC Remote Syslog Schema
note: Field names and the message-ID catalog vary somewhat across iDRAC firmware generations. Items marked "verified": false are reasonable inferences (from documented naming patterns or vendor examples) rather than confirmed line-for-line in Dell's own docs -- confirm against your firmware before scripting against them.

transport.engine: RACLOG (Lifecycle Controller Log / System Event Log)

notes: iDRAC and the syslog server must trust the same CA
iDRAC can present an anonymous TLS identity or a signed identity certificate
Encrypted and unencrypted targets cannot run simultaneously

transport.syslog_pri_severity_note: Most iDRAC generations emit every event at syslog severity Informational (6) regardless of the event's real severity. The true severity travels in the payload's own Severity field, not the PRI byte.

raclog_full_record.used_for: Hardware and Lifecycle Controller events (thermal, power, storage, security, BIOS, licensing, user/audit, firmware jobs, etc.)
raclog_full_record.seen_via: e.g. racadm getraclog, or SIEM-side reconstruction from arg fields

fields.description: Monotonic sequence number of the log entry, unique per iDRAC.
The EEMI message identifier -- a category prefix plus a numeric code.
Alert category the message rolls up to: System Health, Storage, Configuration, Audit, Updates, or Work Notes.
Logging subsystem that generated the record.
The event's real severity: Critical, Warning, Informational, or OK. Authoritative -- not the syslog PRI.
iDRAC local time (or UTC depending on time-zone config) the event was logged.

fields.example: Successfully logged in using john, from 192.168.0.106 and GUI.
fields.description: Fully rendered, human-readable message text with arguments substituted in.
Raw substitution arguments behind the rendered message; matches the registry's ParamTypes/NumberOfArgs.
Fully Qualified Device Descriptor -- the specific component instance the event is about.

raclog_live_syslog_line.used_for: The compact form iDRAC actually streams in real time to a configured remote syslog server
raclog_live_syslog_line.example: Informational, Category: Audit, MessageID: USR0030, Message: Successfully logged in using john, from 192.168.0.106 and GUI.

ism_os_log.used_for: iDRAC Service Module (iSM) events -- the in-OS agent's own audit/health messages, written through the host OS's syslog
ism_os_log.format: <DateTime> <hostname> dsm_ism_srvmgrd[<PID>]: <MessageID> EventID="<id>" EventCategory="Audit" EventSeverity="<severity>" IsPastEvent="<True|False>" language="<locale>" <message text>

fields.description: The managed server's OS hostname (not the iDRAC's).
Fixed process tag for iSM -- filter on this to isolate iSM traffic.
Same severity vocabulary as the main severity list.
True/False -- flags a backfilled event replayed after an iSM restart, vs. one seen live.
Locale of the message text, e.g. en-US.

ism_os_log.prerequisite_setting: iDRAC Service Module installed on the host OS AND OS-to-iDRAC pass-through monitoring enabled (iDRAC Settings -> Services -> iDRAC Service Module -> Enable OS to iDRAC Pass-through). Without this, no iSM events are generated at all.

message_registry.standard: DMTF Redfish Message Registry, served at /redfish/v1/Registries on the iDRAC; the printed EEMI guide is generated from the same catalog
message_registry.message_id_format: RegistryPrefix.Major.Minor.MessageKey (e.g. IDRAC.2.9.USR0030) -- the trailing MessageKey (USR0030) is what appears in the syslog payload

fields.purpose: Family the message belongs to (IDRAC, Base, Manager, Storage, ...) combined with version.
Templated text with %1, %2... placeholders, rendered against arguments.
How many substitution arguments the message expects.
Declared type of each argument (string, number).
The "Recommended Response Action" -- remediation steps, sometimes with the exact RACADM/Redfish/GUI path.
Longer explanation of what triggers the message and likely causes.

severity_levels.meaning: Failure or condition requiring immediate action.
severity_levels.typical_trigger: PSU failure, drive failure, thermal shutdown, security lockout.
Predictive drive failure, redundancy lost, fan above normal, cert expiring.

severity_levels.meaning: Normal operational event, no action needed.
severity_levels.typical_trigger: Login/logout, config change, job started/completed, firmware update result.

severity_levels.meaning: A previously abnormal condition has cleared.
severity_levels.typical_trigger: Redundancy restored, temperature back in range, link back up.
severity_levels.note: Not a selectable filter level in Alert Configuration -- a status transition, not an alert severity you opt into. Enable the category at Informational to receive these.

alert_categories.name: System Health
alert_categories.description: CPU, memory, voltage, temperature, fans, chassis intrusion, GPU/accelerator faults.

alert_categories.name: Storage
alert_categories.description: Controllers, physical/virtual disks, backplanes, predictive failures, rebuilds.

alert_categories.name: Configuration
alert_categories.description: Hardware, firmware, and software configuration changes on the managed system or iDRAC.

alert_categories.name: Audit
alert_categories.description: User authentication, session, and account-management activity.

alert_categories.name: Updates
alert_categories.description: Firmware and driver update job lifecycle -- started, progressing, completed, failed.

alert_categories.name: Work Notes
alert_categories.description: Free-form notes an admin attaches to the log -- not sensor-driven, created deliberately.

message_id_prefixes.subsystem: Security -- certificates, secure boot, chassis intrusion
Logging subsystem itself (log cleared, log full)

message_id_prefixes_note: Deliberately partial -- Dell's per-generation EEMI reference guide documents 100+ prefixes. Control (routing to syslog) is only possible at the alert-category level, not per prefix.

license.note: On Express, the Syslog UI fields exist but delivery silently never happens.

master_alert_switch.purpose: Gates every alert of any kind, regardless of category, severity, or destination
master_alert_switch.web_ui: iDRAC Settings -> Alerts -> Enable Alerts toggle

syslog_destination.purpose: Turns on and points the remote syslog target itself
syslog_destination.redfish: OEM attribute group commonly named SysLog.1 under /redfish/v1/Managers/iDRAC.Embedded.1/Oem/Dell/DellAttributes -- GET the group first, names shift across generations

category_severity_routing.purpose: Decides which category, at which severity, is mirrored specifically to syslog (vs. email/SNMP/IPMI/WS-Eventing/Redfish)
category_severity_routing.web_ui: Configuration -> System Settings -> Alert Configuration (iDRAC9/10) or iDRAC Settings -> Alerts -> Alert Configuration (iDRAC7/8) -- check the Remote Syslog action for each category/severity row
category_severity_routing.racadm_example: racadm eventfilters set -c idrac.alert.system.warning -a none -n snmp,email
category_severity_routing.verified: partial -- idrac.alert.system.* pattern confirmed by Dell; other category keys inferred by the same naming pattern, and the exact 'syslog' action token was not independently confirmed

ism_prerequisite.requirement: iDRAC Service Module installed on the host OS, with OS-to-iDRAC pass-through monitoring enabled
ism_prerequisite.web_ui: iDRAC Settings -> Services -> iDRAC Service Module -> Enable OS to iDRAC Pass-through
